additions.title: Independent Review of NATS (En Route) Plc's Flight Planning System Failure on 28 August 2023: Final report (CAP 2993)
additions.quote: Reverting to manual mode reduces this capacity to approximately 60.
additions.why: Official review of an automated system failing with both primary and backup down. The manual fallback existed and kept flying safe, but handled about 60 flight plans an hour against 700 to 900, and over 700,000 passengers were affected. Shows that a fallback must be sized, not just present. The cover is dated 31 May 2024; the regulator's page gives first publication as 14 November 2024. Not an AI system.

additions.title: SS1/21 Operational resilience: Impact tolerances for important business services
additions.quote: The PRA expects firms to be able to remain within impact tolerances for important business services, irrespective of whether or not they use third parties
additions.why: The prudential regulator's expectations alongside the FCA rule already listed: the recovery target applies whether the service is run in-house or by a supplier, including a supplier within the same group. March 2022 version, updating March 2021. Banks, building societies, designated investment firms and insurers only.

additions.title: Financial Stability in Focus: Artificial intelligence in the financial system
additions.publisher: Bank of England, Financial Policy Committee
additions.locator: Executive summary and the section on operational risks in relation to AI service providers
additions.quote: Growing concentration in the supply of AI-related services could increase risks to the financial system.
additions.why: The UK authority's statement of AI concentration risk: firms rely on vendor-provided models, cloud computing and data aggregators, and the committee expects third-party exposure to keep increasing as models grow more complex. A financial stability view of the financial sector; it sets no requirement on firms.

additions.title: The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence
additions.locator: Executive summary, first bullet; section 4.2.1 and Table 4
additions.quote: The market for these products and services is also highly concentrated
additions.why: International comparator on concentration: reliance on specialised hardware, cloud services and pre-trained models has increased third-party dependencies in AI. A report about the financial sector by an international body; it places no requirements on firms.

additions.title: Principles for Operational Resilience
additions.locator: Principle 3 (business continuity planning and testing); also Principles 5 and 6
additions.quote: Banks should have business continuity plans in place and conduct business continuity exercises
additions.why: The international standard behind the UK rules: continuity plans exercised against severe but plausible scenarios, dependencies on third parties managed, and response and recovery plans kept. Written for banks; it stands in here for ISO 22301, whose own pages refused automated reading.

additions.title: Learning lessons from the cyber-attack: British Library cyber incident review
additions.locator: Section Six, 'Learning lessons from the attack', lesson 6 (page 17 of 18); Section Three on recovery
additions.quote: Business continuity plans for the total outage of all systems need to be practised regularly
additions.why: A public body's own account of recovering from a total systems outage. Its lesson is that plans for a total outage must be practised as well as plans for individual systems, and it found that reliance on legacy systems was the main reason recovery took so long. A self-review by the organisation affected; a ransomware attack, not an AI failure.

additions.title: An Empirical Characterization of Outages and Incidents in Public Services for Large Language Models
additions.quote: Understanding their outages, and particularly measuring their failure-recovery processes, is becoming a stringent problem.
additions.why: Research on the question itself: measures outages and recovery times across eight public large language model services from three providers and finds differences in how long failures take to resolve and how well they are isolated. The abstract records acceptance at the ACM/SPEC performance engineering conference (ICPE 2025); only the abstract page was read. Based on providers' own status reports.

additions.title: Picking on the Same Person: Does Algorithmic Monoculture lead to Outcome Homogenization?
additions.publisher: arXiv (Bommasani, Creel, Kumar, Jurafsky and Liang)
additions.quote: the same systems, or systems that share components (e.g. training data), are deployed by multiple decision-makers
additions.why: Research on concentration from the point of view of the people affected: when many organisations share one model or data source, the same individuals can be failed by all of them. Published at NeurIPS 2022; tested on fairness benchmarks, with mixed results for shared foundation models. About outcomes, not outages.

additions.title: CAA Paper 2004/10: Flight Crew Reliance on Automation
additions.locator: Executive Summary, pages v to vi
additions.quote: has left pilots less proficient in manual skills but still required, on occasions, to take control in time critical situations
additions.why: Evidence on the manual fallback wearing away: a research review for the UK aviation regulator, written at Cranfield University, on crews becoming dependent on automation. It says little structured research existed and relies partly on interviews. From 2004 and from aviation; an analogy for AI, not a study of it.

additions.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
additions.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
additions.locator: Table 4 (MANAGE function), MANAGE 2.3; also Table 1, GOVERN 6.2
additions.quote: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
additions.why: The AI-specific standard for recovery. GOVERN 6.2 adds contingency processes for failures in third-party data or AI systems. Voluntary; a United States framework.

rejected.title: ISO/IEC 42001 and ISO 22301 (standard-setter's own pages)
rejected.reason: HTTP 403 to automated reading, as in the first pass. Not bypassed; no ISO claim made.

rejected.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA), EUR-Lex
rejected.reason: HTTP 202 with an empty body. Not read; no DORA claim made.

rejected.title: Does using artificial intelligence assistance accelerate skill decay and hinder skill development without performers' awareness? (Macnamara et al., Cognitive Research: Principles and Implications, 2024)
rejected.reason: The publisher returned a 'Client Challenge' browser check on the article page and the PDF (also at link.springer.com). Not bypassed, not cited.

rejected.title: AI Foundation Models: Update paper
rejected.reason: Opened (CMA, 11 April 2024). About competition in the supply of foundation models, not continuity for a business that depends on one; the Bank of England and FSB papers make the concentration point more directly.

rejected.title: Principles for operational resilience (address used in the first pass)
rejected.reason: Still returns a web page, not the PDF. The PDF linked from that page was read and is cited instead.

brief_check: Nothing read contradicts the brief. The research log's note that no source addressed loss of manual skill can be updated: the CAA's 2004 paper does, for aviation. No Act was found on legislation.gov.uk for the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill on the date checked.
